mostWorthwhile.text: Building the food web through dung beetles, fertile ground and predator-prey relationships made the connections between waste and feeding tangible without treating organisms as pieces designed to maintain balance.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the watering place was disappointing: its description suggested hunters, but it had no available partners, leaving the next route unclear.

surprise.text: Dung needed insects rather than soil directly; dung beetles then connected it to fertile grassland. That made recycling more specific than I expected.

arbitrary.text: Using air with small furred animals to create scent tracking was not obvious until inspection revealed it, though the explanation made the connection understandable afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see what the connected world does next; the food web suggests consequences beyond individual combinations, and the predator-prey passage avoids an overly tidy account of nature.
